lines.trans: Mom! Oh—Senior Ye-jin?
Oh Seung-chan, my son!
Mom, this is my senior at the network, Producer Tak Ye-jin—and Senior, this is my mother!
Hello, Mother!
Oh heavens, having zero idea you were my son's senior, I was terribly rude—not just once, twice over!
Not at all! Hold on, I will move my car right away—I should have parked head-first, oh gosh I am sorry, I must have been crazy!
No Senior Producer, please do not bother! I was being nosy—it is not like I am the building superintendent!
Not at all, you had every right to speak up!
You even said you were pulling right out, and normally I trust people so easily… please take good care of our Seung-chan!

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + -도 (관리소장도).

examples.text: 아니요 선배님, 안 그러셔도 돼요! 내가 주책이지, 내가 무슨 아파트 관리소장도 아니고!
examples.trans: No Senior Producer, please do not bother! I was being nosy—it is not like I am the building superintendent!
This point about complex superintendent even is really important.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: With future or present-progressive verbs, means 'right away / in a moment'.
With past-tense verbs, means 'just now'.

examples.trans: I'll be right there.
I just arrived a moment ago.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Attributive form of 둘 used directly before counter nouns (두 개, 두 사람).

examples.trans: Please give me two apples.
Let's meet at two o'clock.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?
Is something the matter?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Have you lost your mind? You are driving me crazy—no way!
This expression comes from 'driving me nuts'.

meanings.note: Used as connective -고 (믿고).

examples.text: 신디야, 이제 내가 네 엄마야. 엄마만 믿고 따라오면 돼.
examples.trans: Cindy, from now on I am your mother—just trust Mom and follow me.
Let us do that (trusting and) right away.

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

부탁하다.gloss: I ask you to look after her

meanings.en: I ask you to look after her
meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그러니까 잘 부탁해요, 밖에 맛있는 거 많으니까 식사들 하시고.
examples.trans: So please take good care of her—and enjoy the food outside since there is plenty.
This expression comes from 'I ask you to look after her'.

meanings.note: adverbial form of 빠르다 (to be fast)

examples.trans: Please get ready quickly.
Time goes by so fast.

빼다.gloss: to take out; to remove; to exclude

meanings.en: to take out; to remove; to exclude
meanings.note: Used for removing someone from a schedule or taking something out.
Used in arithmetic.

examples.trans: Please take my name off the list.
I took the key out of my pocket.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (실례를).

examples.text: 어머, 나는 우리 아들 선배님이신지도 모르고 내가 너무 큰 실례를 했어, 한 번도 아니고 두 번씩이나!
examples.trans: Oh heavens, having zero idea you were my son's senior, I was terribly rude—not just once, twice over!
This point about discourtesy, rudeness is really important.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Standard polite negative reply.

examples.trans: No, I'm okay.
No, I haven't eaten yet.
Did you hear about this son?
I was busy today because of son.
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
Test
Test2

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.

meanings.note: Exclamation of surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh my, so nice to meet you!
Oh my, I left my phone behind.

meanings.note: Used as honorific noun + topic (어머님은).

examples.text: 저희 어머님은 가수 전영록 씨 노래를 들으면 아직도 옛날 연애하던 좋았던 시절이 생각나서 가슴이 떨리고 좋으시답니다.
examples.trans: Whenever my mother hears singer Jeon Young-rok's songs, her heart still flutters happily remembering the sweet days when she was young and in love.
This point about mother is really important.

meanings.note: affectionate/informal word for mother

examples.trans: I went to the market with my mum.
The food my mum makes is the most delicious.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: describes how things typically work
refers to an initial state or plan

examples.trans: Traffic is usually heavy on Mondays.
This place was originally a park.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.
One moment please, let me swap the camera battery.
The topic of just a moment came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Humble 1st person plural pronoun used when speaking to superiors or in formal settings.

examples.trans: We will prepare first.
Welcome to our company.
Did you hear about this to the forefront?
I was busy today because of to the forefront.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Respectful, polite adjective used to apologize in workplaces and to strangers. Formal 죄송합니다 is the standard workplace apology. RR: joesonghada.

examples.trans: I am very sorry for being late.
I am sorry for the inconvenience.

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (주차를).

examples.text: 아닙니다! 잠시만요 제가 차를 빨리 뺄게요, 전면 주차를 했어야 되는데 어머 죄송해요 제가 미쳤나 봐요!
examples.trans: Not at all! Hold on, I will move my car right away—I should have parked head-first, oh gosh I am sorry, I must have been crazy!
This point about parking is really important.

meanings.note: Used as noun + copula + -지 (주책이지,).

examples.text: 아니요 선배님, 안 그러셔도 돼요! 내가 주책이지, 내가 무슨 아파트 관리소장도 아니고!
examples.trans: No Senior Producer, please do not bother! I was being nosy—it is not like I am the building superintendent!
This point about was being meddlesome is really important.

meanings.note: Short for 자동차.

examples.trans: This is my father's car.
I parked the car in the parking lot.
It really is is loud, so compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is is loud, so and nice.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour
My office is close to home.
I go to work at the office at 9 a.m.
